title: See it or set it?
hook: Filtering a variable and forcing its value can select different worlds.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: set do(X = x) in a simulated system and compare it with filtering for X = x.

misconception: Treating intervene as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: set do(X = x) in a simulated system and compare it with filtering for X = x.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Let fair binary Z generate X=Z and Y=2X+4Z. If you intervene to set X=1, what mean Y follows?
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-intervene/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Z fairbinary; X=Z (observational), Y=2X+4Z. Filter X=1 givesY6 vsX0 gives0. Intervene X1 averagesY4; interveneX0 averagesY2, causaldifference2.

claims.text: Setting X=1 retains mean Y=4; selecting observed X=1 retains Y=6. Intervention leaves both values of Z represented, while selection identifies Z=1 in this model.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-intervene/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Z fairbinary; X=Z (observational), Y=2X+4Z. Filter X=1 givesY6 vsX0 gives0. Intervene X1 averagesY4; interveneX0 averagesY2, causaldifference2.

claims.text: The difference comes from cutting Z→X rather than conditioning on X. The causal effect of setting X from 0 to 1 is 2, even though the observed group gap is 6.
claims.source: src/demos/probability/p100-intervene/spec.ts; exact finite illustration specified in manager numericCase: Z fairbinary; X=Z (observational), Y=2X+4Z. Filter X=1 givesY6 vsX0 gives0. Intervene X1 averagesY4; interveneX0 averagesY2, causaldifference2.

claims.text: If Z confounds X and Y, is selecting X=1 generally the same operation as forcing X=1? Selection can change the upstream-Z mix; intervention replaces the X assignment rule.
